scope: Hodgson-linked paper-pulp transfers with material/package state, route infrastructure, Company transport metrology, and documentary/archival routing.
central_claim: The March 1842 twenty-four-package pulp shipment moved through two linked infrastructures: a physical transport regime and a documentary-administrative regime. The physical route remains unresolved, but the document search can now be split into upstream Halliday directive branches, the secure Champaran incoming-register witness, a downstream Woodcock reply/bill branch, and possible Patna/Calcutta receipt branches. Halliday's 1842 dual secretariat roles prevent assignment of the initiating instruction to one department without a direct record.

multi_metrology_model.interpretation: Material circulation becomes administratively actionable through multiple non-equivalent metrologies layered around the object. Package count does not equal mass; route allowance does not equal observed duration; boat capacity does not reveal the actual boat used.

documentary_state_model.interpretation: Material movement can generate a parallel documentary circulation. Administrative handoffs distribute recoverable traces across sender, recipient, accounting, proceeding and receipt systems; the documentary route should therefore be reconstructed node by node rather than treated as a single missing-file problem.

source_control_rules: Do not use the 1825 two-month allowance as actual 1842 transit duration.
Do not claim the 1825 allowance remained unchanged in 1842 without later rules or the actual freight bill.
Do not infer boat capacity from 24-package count or package mass from Company baggage-boat categories.
Keep standard allowance, actual time, standard rate and actual cost separate.
Keep Govindgunge/Govind Gunge/Govind Gang exact strings in source fields.
Keep Halliday identity secure but initiating department unresolved.
Do not collapse Government of Bengal and Government of India Halliday roles into one archival branch.
Treat IOR/P/13/39 as an early-1842 candidate Bengal Proceedings container, not a proven pulp file.
Treat West Bengal State Archives General Department proceedings as a candidate series until a consignment-level paper-pulp record is found.
Do not infer the 1842 Champaran incoming-register volume number from the 1839 Vol. 6 witness.
Use the 1859-1862 Champaran Register of Letters Issued only as later evidence of an outgoing record form, not proof of identical 1842 survival.
Keep public-web non-recovery separate from archival non-survival.
Keep the Serampore consignment edge unproven until a receipt, forwarding instruction, matching package count or other consignment-level identifier is recovered.
